answer: Divergent Challenge Ledger: each identity must answer a random hidden challenge whose answer depends on its private history, and publish the reply hash as a comet-like beacon every round. Clones, unable to diverge, must broadcast identical hashes; the ledger flags any island of duplicate hash streams and severs it. To survive, an attacker must run a separate challenge history per clone, paying one full ledger-sync and challenge cost per identity, forever standing on that ledge of recurring compute and storage.
